Face — her own: a mature, poised woman; porcelain-pale skin; diamond-shaped face; medium-sized eyes — wide almond eyes, outer eye corners slightly lifted; thin arched brows; straight narrow nose; full heart-shaped lips; honey-gold eyes; dark berry lipstick.

Her element, carried in her design: arsenic: the patient, elegant poison — white arsenic, the 'inheritance powder' of whispered court intrigues, until James Marsh's test of 1836 caught it as a dark silvery mirror on porcelain; Scheele's green of 1775, the dazzling poison-emerald pigment that papered nineteenth-century parlours; golden orpiment and red-orange realgar, ancient pigments it forms with sulfur; Salvarsan of 1910, the first 'magic bullet' drug; a steel-grey metalloid that skips melting and sublimes with a smell of garlic; poison and cure held in one smiling hand.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — MECHA

Steel-grey and porcelain-white armor with poison-emerald and golden-orpiment trim, a symmetrical pair of slender mechanical sub-arms reaching from her back, ending in fine dropper and scalpel-like tools and small glass vials, red-orange realgar indicator lights; elegant, patient, poison and cure; her own two human arms stay as they are; the plates must read as solid armor, not a gown.
Silhouette: a symmetrical pair of mechanical sub-arms reaching out from her back, ending in shields or tools — her own two human arms stay as they are. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette.
Colours: poison-emerald Scheele's green, golden orpiment yellow, realgar orange-red, metallic steel grey, porcelain white.
Exposure (bold): her mecha frame is cut open by design in only these places — bare shoulders and upper arms between pauldron and gauntlet, and a deep open chest window with natural cleavage framed by the chest plates; everywhere else she stays fully plated. The plates stay on, fitted and symmetrical, with skin clearly showing in each opening. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; keep the plate material and palette.

4. SCENE

Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: the scene's own light, rendered the way this style renders light and skin.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (As) and atomic number (33) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish.
